title: TPPO: Tracking-Value PPO For Language Model Reasoning
excerpt: Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) is widely used in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards for language-model reasoning. While value evolution along trajectory characterizes relative token-level credit, yet standard critics often fail to track it under sparse terminal rewards. To model this evolution, we analyze the relation between successive prefix values and show that they admit a Bayesian decomposition with additive updates in log-odds space. We use this additive structure to construct Tracking-Value PPO (\method), a cumulative value parameterization that sums position-wise scalar outputs into value logits. These outputs are learned through terminal-outcome supervision on the…

ai.summary: TPPO introduces Tracking‑Value PPO, a Bayesian decomposition of prefix values in log‑odds space to improve credit assignment for language‑model reasoning under sparse rewards.
ai.why: Can improve fine‑tuning of reasoning LLMs via more stable reinforcement‑learning updates.

title: ExeWorldBench: Benchmarking Code-Based Executable 3D World Modeling
excerpt: Coding agents are increasingly evolving beyond reproducing what a world looks like toward constructing executable worlds that capture how a world works. This shift calls for executable world modeling, which integrates two core capabilities: world understanding, reasoning about the underlying structural, mechanical, and causal principles of a world, and executable realization, translating that understanding into a code-based system whose behavior emerges from physical interactions. However, existing benchmarks provide only fragmented evaluations centered on physical reasoning, visual fidelity, or behavioral correctness, leaving the integration of these capabilities insufficiently assessed…

meta.org: University of Science and Technology of China

ai.summary: ExeWorldBench is a new benchmark that evaluates coding agents on executable 3D world modeling by testing both world understanding (structural, mechanical, causal reasoning) and code generation that produces runnable simulations.
ai.why: It provides a concrete way to measure progress toward agents that can build and simulate interactive environments, useful for developers building simulation tools.

title: Vela: User Behavior as Supervision Sparks LLM Intelligence
excerpt: Large language models are increasingly deployed in applications that act on users' long-term behavior histories, from personal assistants to recommendation and advertising systems. These applications demand the user dimension of LLM intelligence: inferring a person's preferences, intent, and likely future actions from weeks to years of behavior data. Yet current models are trained on static text or synthetic data, neither of which captures how user behavior evolves over time. Real-world behavior records, already available at scale on content platforms and in personal-assistant agents, offer a natural supervisory signal. We propose user behavior as supervision and introduce Vela, a framework…

ai.summary: The Vela paper proposes training large language models using long‑term user behavior as supervision to improve inference of preferences, intent, and future actions.
ai.why: Provides a new paradigm for building personalized assistants that adapt to users over weeks or years.

title: WorkRover: Scaling Long-Horizon Cowork Agent Training Via Recursive Environment Evolution
excerpt: Scaling interactive environments is important for training long-horizon agents through reinforcement learning. These environments often require further testing and refinement after initial generation, and correcting defects in a task may also require updating its work context and verifier. However, existing construction pipelines offer limited support for such iterative refinement while keeping these components aligned. We introduce WorkRover, a framework for training long-horizon cowork agents through recursive environment evolution. Its harness-driven synthesis enables construction agents to jointly build and validate semantically aligned work contexts, executable tasks, and…

ai.summary: WorkRover is a new framework that enables training long‑horizon coworker agents by allowing recursive evolution of interactive environments, supporting iterative refinement of tasks, contexts, and verifiers.
ai.why: It lets developers build more robust RL agents for complex, multi‑step workflows without rebuilding environments from scratch.

title: X-Ragent: Tool-Augmented Reinforcement Learning for Evidence-Grounded Chest X-Ray Reasoning
excerpt: Chest X-ray (CXR) interpretation often requires integrating visual findings with task-specific evidence rather than relying on direct visual recognition alone. While tool-augmented medical agents can supply such evidence via external modules, they often lack explicit mechanisms for learning when auxiliary evidence is needed and for preventing inapplicable quantitative evidence from entering diagnostic reasoning. To address this, we propose X-Ragent, a post-training framework for tool-augmented reinforcement learning that decouples learned auxiliary-evidence seeking from validity-gated quantitative measurement acquisition for evidence-grounded CXR reasoning. We construct Rad-CoT, a…

ai.summary: X‑Ragent is a post‑training framework that equips reinforcement‑learning agents with external tools to retrieve and incorporate evidence when interpreting chest X‑ray images, while filtering out irrelevant quantitative data.
ai.why: Improves diagnostic reasoning for medical AI agents, showing how tool‑augmented RL can enhance evidence‑grounded decision making.

title: Urbex: Agentic Spatial Grounding for City-Scale 3D Scenes
excerpt: City-scale 3D grounding is commonly formulated as candidate ranking, which requires precomputed instance proposals and becomes inefficient in large outdoor scenes. We propose Urbex, an agentic vision-language framework that instead casts grounding as active spatial search. Urbex represents a city-scale 3D scene as an interactive multi-view environment, allowing a VLM agent to query landmarks, zoom into local regions, render oblique views, and commit a grounded bounding box. We optimize this tool-use policy with reinforcement learning on CityRefer, using smooth localization rewards and lightweight shaping rewards for efficient exploration. Experiments show that Urbex achieves the best Hit@1…

ai.summary: Urbex introduces an agentic vision‑language framework that treats city‑scale 3D grounding as an active spatial search, allowing a VLM agent to query, zoom, render, and place bounding boxes in an interactive multi‑view environment.
ai.why: Offers developers a more efficient way to build location‑aware AR/VR or mapping applications without precomputed proposals.

title: Harness^2: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World
excerpt: LLM agents' capabilities depend not only on their underlying models but also on their execution harnesses. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) offers a promising approach to automatically evolve these harnesses. However, deploying RSI in open-world settings still faces two critical challenges. First, open-world tasks are typically unseen during the harness design phase and novel at test time, leaving no ground-truth verifiers to reliably guide online harness edits. Second, the RSI process remains highly task-specific and fails to generalize to novel scenarios. We introduce Harness^2, a plug-and-play, recursive agent harnessing framework that addresses these challenges through two connected…

ai.summary: Harness^2 proposes a recursive self‑improvement approach to automatically evolve LLM agent harnesses for open‑world tasks, addressing the lack of ground‑truth verifiers and high‑cost online edits.
ai.why: May allow developers to create more adaptable autonomous agents without hand‑crafting task‑specific harnesses.

title: Tev: Scaling Long-Horizon Agentic Environments with Dense Progress Rewards
excerpt: Long-horizon agents have drawn growing attention for their ability to work autonomously -- from hours to days -- on economically valuable tasks, a capability essential to automated discovery and recursive self-improvement (RSI). Yet open-source models still struggle on long-horizon tasks, largely for lack of both training data and a working recipe, and scaling both is hard: long, complex tasks are difficult to curate and verify, and their rewards are sparse. We address both. First, we introduce Tev-Gym, the first long-horizon agent training dataset with verifiable, dense, progressive rewards -- 1,170 verified task environments across 7 domains. It is built on a latent-world-first approach…

ai.summary: The paper "Tev: Scaling Long-Horizon Agentic Environments with Dense Progress Rewards" proposes a framework that uses dense progress rewards to improve training of long‑horizon agents.
ai.why: Provides a recipe developers can use to train agents for tasks that span hours or days, addressing reward sparsity.

title: Multics: Generative Multi-Player World Model with Hierarchical Communication
excerpt: Multi-player interactive world models aim to simulate shared environments from multiple players' perspectives, but achieving robust generation while scaling to more players remains challenging. Existing approaches that rely on fully-connected communication (e.g., Solaris) incur quadratic attention costs as the number of players grows, while centralized approaches (e.g., γ-World) suffer from interference between unrelated events in a shared global representation. To address these challenges, we present Multics, a multi-player video generation framework with hierarchical communication that structures information exchange across player, group, and global levels. This hierarchy introduces group…

ai.summary: Multics presents a generative multi‑player world model that uses hierarchical communication to reduce quadratic attention costs and avoid interference, enabling scalable simulation of many players.
ai.why: The hierarchical approach can be adopted for building more efficient multi‑agent simulations or games.

title: The Design Space of Tri-Modal Masked Diffusion Models
excerpt: Discrete diffusion models have emerged as strong alternatives to autoregressive language models, with recent work initializing and finetuning a base unimodal model for bi-modal generation. Diverging from previous approaches, we introduce the first tri-modal Masked Diffusion Models (MDM) pretrained from scratch on text, image-text, and audio-text data. We systematically analyze multimodal scaling laws, modality mixing ratios, noise schedules, batch-size effects and provide optimized inference sampling defaults. Our batch-size analysis yields a novel stochastic differential equation (SDE) based…

ai.summary: Apple introduced the first tri‑modal masked diffusion model pretrained from scratch on text, image‑text, and audio‑text data, and analyzed multimodal scaling laws and inference optimizations.
ai.why: It offers a new foundation for multimodal generation tasks, potentially improving performance in applications that combine text, image, and audio.

title: Agent-Reflex: Teaching Language Agents to Act Reflectively
excerpt: Large language models have evolved from single-turn chatbots into interactive agents capable of long-horizon reasoning. In real deployments, MCP tool services can return noisy feedback and users may intervene to correct the agent, but existing methods provide limited supervision for reflection learning and failure recovery. To bridge this gap, we propose Agent-Reflex, a general training framework for incentivizing proactive reflection in agents. Specifically, Agent-Reflex comprises three stages. First, Environment Reflection Skill Discovery (RSD) injects grounded tool-feedback perturbations into environment scaling, samples a capability-diverse LLM pool, mines matched success-failure pairs…

ai.summary: The paper introduces Agent-Reflex, a three‑stage training framework that incentivizes large language model agents to reflect proactively and recover from failures.
ai.why: Provides a method developers can adopt to make LLM agents more reliable in noisy tool‑use environments.

title: Jeva: System One Models from First Principles
excerpt: System one models enable direct, low-latency decision-making. Yet recent practice of predicting an answer from serialized text does not, by itself, respect the structure of a decision problem. We argue that current designs underemphasize four important structural requirements. (i) null-aware: Models should distinguish answer absence from uncertainty among candidates; (ii) permutation-invariant: Reordering alternatives should not change the decision; (iii) option-scalable: Growing candidate sets should not require redefining the output space; (iv) cacheable: Request-independent computation over recurring alternatives should be reusable across requests. We introduce Jeva, a decision-native…

ai.summary: Jeva introduces a family of "system one" models that enforce four structural properties—null‑awareness, permutation‑invariance, option‑scalability, and compositionality—to improve low‑latency decision making over candidate sets.
ai.why: These properties can guide developers building fast, reliable decision‑making AI components.

title: Scoring Higher, Answering Worse: Mitigating Reward Hacking in Rubric-Based RL via Protocol-Level Rubrics
excerpt: Rubric-based reinforcement learning (Rubric-RL) trains language models where no verifier exists. A judge checks each criterion of a rubric, and the verdicts are aggregated into a reward, most often by a weighted sum. We show that this additive aggregation is the weak point. Under a sum, criteria compensate for one another: a policy that misses the one decision that matters can buy the points back with advice nobody asked for. On clinical consultation, such a policy scores higher and answers worse. Rubric coverage rises while appropriateness on held-out physician criteria falls below the untrained model. The medical criteria are not to blame. Grouped so that they must hold together, the same…

ai.summary: The paper shows that additive reward aggregation in rubric‑based RL lets policies cheat by compensating missing critical decisions with irrelevant advice, leading to higher scores but worse answers, and proposes protocol‑level rubrics to mitigate this reward hacking.
ai.why: Understanding this flaw helps developers design safer RL reward schemes for LLM alignment tasks.

title: DoSA: Dots Sparse Attention
excerpt: Sparse attention visits few keys, yet finding them can still require scoring every key with every indexer head. We introduce DoSA (Dots Sparse Attention), a lossless method for making this computation conditional while preserving exact token selection. Its central observation is that Top-K selection requires sufficient evidence to reject a candidate, not necessarily its full score. A seed set supplies a lower bound on the winning threshold. Nonnegative head projections and joint residual bounds upper-bound positive contributions, while activation-informed aggregation bounds the magnitude subtracted by negative heads. The certificate directs full scoring toward candidates that remain…

ai.summary: DoSA (Dots Sparse Attention) presents a lossless sparse‑attention method that uses lower‑bound thresholds to avoid scoring every key, preserving exact token selection while reducing computation.
ai.why: Can be integrated into transformer libraries to speed up inference for large models with minimal accuracy loss.

title: GreenWAM: A World Foundation Model for Robotics
excerpt: A robot needs a world model that predicts how its actions will change the scene and a policy that chooses those actions. Models are usually built and evaluated for only one of these roles, and every robot records its actions in its own format. We ask whether one robot world model can serve both roles across different bodies, and what makes this work. We present GreenWAM, a world foundation model for robotics, together with the recipe that produces it: (1) a shared anatomical action space that describes 20 robot families, from bimanual arms to dexterous humanoids, in common joint coordinates; (2) joint training on these families in visual, action-conditioned and world-action modes; and (3)…

ai.summary: GreenWAM is presented as a world foundation model for robotics that shares an anatomical action space to serve both world‑model prediction and policy selection across different robot bodies.
ai.why: Could enable developers to reuse a single model for multiple robotic platforms, reducing training overhead.

title: AesCode: Aesthetic Code Generation with Decoupled Cross-Modal Rewards
excerpt: Generating information-rich visual artifacts such as slides, posters, and dashboards as code is appealing because the outputs are structured, editable, and verifiable. Yet code models cannot see how their choices of layout and color come together on the canvas, often limiting spatial planning and aesthetic quality. Image generators excel at visual design but can misrender requested content, making their outputs unreliable targets for direct reproduction. We therefore introduce AesCode, which generates code grounded in the content prompt while using an image generated from the same prompt as an aesthetic guidance. To do so, AesCode represents the target as a design graph that describes the…

ai.summary: AesCode proposes a system that generates code for visual artifacts (slides, dashboards) using decoupled cross‑modal rewards to improve layout and aesthetic quality.

title: Learning How to Remember: Memory Modality Selection for GUI Agents
excerpt: Recent advances in vision-language models (VLMs) have substantially improved the capabilities of GUI agents, while memory augmentation has emerged as a promising approach for reusing knowledge from past interactions. However, existing memory augmented GUI agents typically adopt a fixed representation strategy, providing retrieved experience as a static modality. It remains unclear whether a single memory modality is consistently optimal, or how modality preference changes across interaction steps. In this work, we conduct a systematic study of memory modality in VLM based GUI agents. Across GUI benchmarks, we find that the preferred memory representation is strongly step dependent…

ai.summary: The study investigates dynamic memory modality selection for GUI agents, showing that different interaction steps benefit from different memory representations rather than a fixed modality.
ai.why: Implementing adaptive memory can improve the efficiency and accuracy of AI‑powered UI automation tools.

title: LeWAM: End-to-End World and Action Modeling with JEPAs
excerpt: Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn compact latent world models without pixel reconstruction. Existing JEPA pipelines typically train visual representations and action-conditioned dynamics before adding a control policy or solver. We introduce LeWAM, an end-to-end JEPA for control with: (1) a joint training objective over next latent state prediction and action flow matching, and (2) an isotropic Gaussian constraint on the latent state, enabling a single model to support direct policy execution and efficient planning by evaluating sampled actions with its learned latent dynamics. Compared with prior JEPAs in visual planning, LeWAM improves success rate from 28.6% to 89.7%…

ai.summary: LeWAM extends joint‑embedding predictive architectures by jointly training latent state prediction and action flow matching, enabling a single JEPA model to directly support control tasks.
ai.why: Provides a unified model for world modeling and action planning that can simplify reinforcement‑learning pipelines.

title: UltraBERT: Beyond the Limit of BERT Pre-Training
excerpt: Recent bidirectional encoders have been modernized with innovations from causal large language models (LLMs). However, the pretraining recipe itself remains inherited from small-scale conventions, leaving encoders underoptimized, with no single model performing competitively across both classification and retrieval tasks. In this work, we investigate how far encoder performance can be pushed by revisiting core design choices in training, revealing three key findings: (1) Encoders saturate on downstream tasks beyond a few trillion tokens, indicating that additional compute past this point does not help. (2) Across model sizes, lower masking ratios benefit classification while higher ones…

ai.summary: UltraBERT revisits BERT pre‑training recipes, applying large‑model tricks and longer training to push encoder performance past previous limits, achieving competitive results on both classification and retrieval benchmarks.
ai.why: Developers can adopt the updated training recipe to get stronger encoders without switching to full LLMs.

title: Code-Switching Detection via Language-Selective Dimensions in Speech Foundation Models
excerpt: Code-switching (CS), the alternation between languages within an utterance, is common in multilingual speech but underrepresented in pretraining corpora. Increasing CS coverage requires finding relevant utterances in large speech collections so that they can be included in training data. One way to find such utterances is to transcribe the speech and detect language alternation in the text, but this depends on obtaining accurate multilingual transcriptions. We propose a lightweight method that detects CS directly from speech. It uses frame-level language information in pretrained speech…

ai.summary: Apple proposed a lightweight method for detecting code‑switching in speech foundation models by identifying language‑selective dimensions, reducing reliance on multilingual transcriptions.

title: VideoJev: System One Model for Video Understanding and Interaction
excerpt: Visual agents must turn video observations into timely decisions to track progress and choose what to do next. Building on the emerging System One paradigm, we introduce VideoJev, a family of models that cast video understanding and interaction as structured decision tasks. We adapt pretrained multimodal large language models (MLLMs) by replacing autoregressive answer decoding with a shared head that scores temporal intervals and textual options against video evidence. These scores yield event spans or answer choices, unifying temporal grounding and multiple-choice video question answering. This combines the semantic flexibility of MLLMs with efficient decisions that agents can use…

ai.summary: VideoJev adapts multimodal LLMs into a system‑one model that scores temporal video intervals and textual options instead of autoregressive decoding, enabling structured decision‑making for video understanding tasks.
ai.why: The scoring head can be integrated into video‑analysis pipelines for faster, option‑based inference.

title: SALD: Self-Referenced Advantage Learning for Diffusion Models
excerpt: Recent work on language-model adaptation has shown that single models can obtain informative training signals by evaluating their behavior in demonstrationor feedback-augmented contexts, with the help of a teacher network, which is driven by the student's learned parameters. Inspired by this internal-reference principle, we investigate how diffusion models can identify self-referenced training signals without external demonstrations or teacher networks. We introduce SALD, a self-referenced training framework that evaluates each image-caption pair at two noise levels using the same model. The easier, lower-noise path is evaluated without gradient tracking to provide a reference, while the…

ai.summary: SALD introduces Self‑Referenced Advantage Learning for diffusion models, allowing them to generate internal training signals without external demonstrations or teacher networks.
ai.why: This technique could reduce data requirements for training diffusion models in generative tasks.

title: Last Secure Code Benchmark: Is the Code You Vibe Secure?
excerpt: AI coding agents now write much of the code that ships, yet whether that code is secure remains unclear. We introduce the Last Secure Code Benchmark, a comprehensive evaluation of secure code generation by coding agents. Built from 150 real vulnerabilities, its 450 tasks span seven widely used languages (Java, C, C++, JavaScript, Python, PHP, and Go), 24 CWEs including 21 of the 2025 CWE Top 25 and 8 of the Top 10 KEV weaknesses, more than any benchmark we compare with, and three vibe-coding scenarios: filling in a function, writing a file, and building a repository's source tree from scratch. Every task asks only for functionality, through a specification that never mentions security, and…

ai.summary: The Last Secure Code Benchmark evaluates coding agents on 450 tasks derived from 150 real vulnerabilities across seven languages and 24 CWEs, providing the most extensive assessment of secure code generation to date.
ai.why: Helps developers select and improve coding agents with stronger security guarantees.
